plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated tempo run for lactate threshold development.
Long runs are longer, more closely mimicking race distances.
More varied workout types (long, tempo, easy) target different aspects of fitness.
plan_b_advantages: More consistent easy running volume, potentially beneficial for building a solid aerobic base.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more targeted approach to building aerobic capacity and lactate threshold through structured tempo runs and longer, sustained efforts. Plan B, while focusing on consistent easy running, lacks the specific intensity work needed to truly improve speed and efficiency on trails. Plan A’s inclusion of a 10km tempo run at a controlled effort is crucial for developing the kind of sustained power required for faster times, whereas Plan B’s tempo session is shorter and less demanding. Furthermore, Plan A’s longer long runs (131 minutes) better simulate the demands of a typical trail race, building resilience and adaptation to the terrain.
